 The golf influencer endured a difficult spell on the course during 2026 competition
 The American influencer and former golfer Paige Spiranac LAPRESSE 
 DAVID SCHIAVONE (SAM)
 Editor Editor Updated 12/11/2026

 Paige Spiranac has given her followers a reason to smile after a frustrating experience at the 2026 Internet Invitational.
 Rather than disappearing from social media following her latest setback, the golf personality returned with a simple selfie and an even shorter message: “Hi.”
 Paige Spiranac heats up the kitchen as she reveals her ‘liquid gold’ breakfast secret The November 11 post quickly attracted attention from fans, many of whom were pleased to see her back online after a difficult tournament appearance.
 The response also marked a contrast with the aftermath of last year's competition, when Spiranac found herself at the center of a heated rules controversy.
 This time, the discussion surrounding her performance has been much more straightforward.
 Spiranac was unhappy with her golf, particularly during the fourth episode of the Internet Invitational, where she struggled with a spell of poor ball-striking that she described as the yips and the shanks.
 “If you ever wonder what the swing yips look like on the course then watch me play in episode 4 of the Internet Invitational lol I caught a nasty case of the shanks right before and never recovered. One of the worst 9 holes I’ve ever played, but that’s golf for you,” she posted on X.
 She was equally candid about how the experience felt while she was playing: “I was in a dark, dark place out there.”
 However, Spiranac was also keen to show that she could take the disappointment in stride. Reflecting on whether the performance had brought her to tears, she added: “No tears were shed. By evidence of last year you know when I’m crying.”
 Her latest selfie suggests that, at least publicly, she is choosing to move forward rather than dwell on the result.
 Memories of 2025 tournament controversy
 The Internet Invitational became a major talking point in 2025 when Spiranac 's team reached the final of the inaugural $1 million competition. During the deciding match, she was accused of improving her teammate Malosi Togisala 's lie by pressing down grass near his ball.
 Spiranac said she hadn't realized that the action could constitute a rules violation and insisted she had no intention of cheating. The incident attracted intense online criticism, with the influencer later describing the abuse she received as among the worst of her career.
 She explained that the backlash had become so overwhelming that she needed to step away from social media for her mental health. In a later video, she said she had received thousands of hostile messages, including death threats.
 There's been no comparable cheating allegation surrounding her 2026 performance. Instead, the focus has been on a golfer openly acknowledging that she had played poorly.
 The 2026 edition is also considerably bigger, with a reported $4 million prize pool and a field of online golf personalities and other well-known names.
 The competition, organized around the creator-golf world associated with Barstool Sports and Bob Does Sports , has been released as a series of episodes rather than a conventional live tournament.
